newsitem.title: USA: British nanny may face murder charge, infant dead.
newsitem.headline: British nanny may face murder charge, infant dead.

text.p: A nine-month old infant suffering from shaken-baby syndrome, died late on Sunday night and his British nanny was expected to face murder charges as soon as on Monday.
A spokeswoman at Children's Hospital in Boston said the infant, Matthew Eatten, died shortly after 11 p.m. EST (0400 GMT on Monday) from injuries to the brain.
Prosecutors charged Louise Woodward, 18, of Chester, England, with assault and battery for allegedly shaking the baby so violently he suffered head trauma.
Assistant District Attorney Lynn Rooney said after a court hearing on Friday, that if the child died, she would seek to have murder charges filed against Woodward.
"If the baby should not survive, the Commonwealth will seek a murder indictment," Rooney told reporters after the Friday hearing.
Matthew Eatten died from "an intracranial haemorrhage," according to hospital spokeswoman Lisa Cohen. The infant was kept on life-support after he arrived at the hospital last Tuesday.
Woodward, who arrived in the United States in June 1996 from England, has been living with and working for the child's parents since November, according to court records.
